title: Concierge-style enterprise intake and lightweight scoping proxy for Sales/CS
creator: Nina Kapoor
description:
Problem: Sales and CS frequently surface enterprise feature asks that are heavy on context (compliance, regional hosting, throughput guarantees) but lack standardized signals to prioritize and scope. Current handoffs are ad hoc: Slack threads, spreadsheet notes, and lengthy syncs. That causes long discovery cycles, missed enterprise deals, and duplicated effort across PM/Eng/Design.

Proposal: Build a lightweight 'concierge' intake layer operated by CS/Sales that standardizes required fields, auto-classifies asks into 'scope proxies' (e.g., M1: low-effort UI tweak, M2: runtime config, M3: Dedicated/private deployment integration), and produces a one-page scoping proxy that includes: business context, technical constraints, non-functional requirements, suggested rollout pattern, and a risk bucket. The concierge will be an intermediate artifact (not a full PRD) to enable fast prioritization meetings and reduce back-and-forth.

Scope: 1) Define intake form template and classification rules. 2) Implement a Google Form + Airtable/Drive template + Slackbot notifier for beta. 3) Draft scoping proxy template and acceptance criteria. 4) Run trial with 3 strategic CS reps and 2 AE teams. 5) Collect metrics and iterate before building a Console-integrated intake flow.

Key trade-offs: Start with manual/templated flow to avoid product build cost; accept some manual review load initially. Rely on human-in-the-loop classification to maintain signal quality vs premature automation. Focus on conversion-to-deal and time-to-decision as primary success metrics versus engineering throughput reduction in this phase.
acceptance_criteria: Concierge intake template finalized and documented in Confluence
Automated notification to #pm-enterprise channel for every submission
Scoping proxy created for 80% of submitted asks within 48 hours
Pilot with 3 CS reps and 2 AE teams completed with feedback logged
Baseline metrics collected: time-to-first-scope, conversion-to-RFC, and estimated engineering points
